html:
The Kalapalo are an Indigenous people of the Upper Xingu River in Mato Grosso, Brazil, one of the many peoples who share the Upper Xingu way of life. They speak a Cariban language, close to that of their neighbours the Kuikuro, and numbered 569 in 2010.

The Upper Xingu peoples speak different languages but share ceremonies, trade and marriage, and settle disputes through wrestling and ritual rather than war. The best known ceremony is the Kuarup, which honours the dead. Their land lies inside the Xingu Indigenous Park, set up in 1961 through the work of the Villas-Bôas brothers. The Panará were moved into the park in 1975, and the Kayapó live to the north.
